detail.longDescription: I'm happy to announce Gitview 0.1.0, my fast, native, screen-reader-first GitHub client for Windows. I've been living in it for my own GitHub work for a while now, and I think it's finally in good enough shape for other people to use too. What it does: Notifications, your repositories, stars, watched repos, things assigned to you, and review requests, each in its own view. Filter and sort each one however you want, and it remembers. Open an issue or pull request and read the whole thread as a list, one post per line, with Enter to read a post formatted. Comment, close as completed, not planned, or duplicate, reopen, mark notifications done, star, watch, and copy links. Open any repository to read its commits on any branch, plus its open and closed issues and pull requests. Ctrl+G takes owner/name, a link, or just a bare name for one of your own, like gh does. Ctrl+U opens anyone's profile, with their repos, stars, followers, and who they follow, most recent first. Templates for what every list item says, Fedra style, so you can make it read exactly how you want. Every shortcut is customizable, and Ctrl+Alt+G hides it to the tray and brings it back from anywhere, along with whatever dialog you had open. It automagically updates itself, and you can choose between releases and dev builds of every commit. It's written in Rust with wxDragon, using pretty much every Accessware crate I've put out lately, so the lists don't get reread out from under you when things refresh among other nice things. There are portable zips and installers for both X64 and ARM64 Windows, and a full manual is in the zip and under Help. Huge thanks to everyone who sent ideas along the way, keep them coming! https:// github.com/accessware/gitview/ releases/tag/v0.1.0 # GitHub # accessibility # rust
